title: Reading Practice 9 - The Evolution of Music
description: IELTS Academic Reading practice about how music has changed from ancient times to the digital age.

stimuli.title: Passage 1: The Evolution of Music
stimuli.content:
A Music is one of the oldest and most universal forms of human expression. Archaeological evidence suggests that humans have been making music for at least 40,000 years. The oldest known musical instruments are bone flutes discovered in caves in Germany, dating to approximately 35,000 BCE. These flutes were carefully crafted with precisely spaced finger holes, indicating a sophisticated understanding of musical scales even at this early date.

B The development of musical notation in the medieval period transformed music from a purely oral tradition into something that could be precisely recorded and reproduced. The system of staff notation that we use today was largely developed by Guido d'Arezzo, an Italian monk, in the 11th century. This innovation allowed composers to create increasingly complex works and enabled music to be distributed widely. The invention of the printing press further accelerated the spread of written music across Europe.

C The 20th century brought perhaps the most dramatic changes in the history of music. The invention of recording technology, beginning with Thomas Edison's phonograph in 1877, meant that music could be captured and replayed for the first time. Radio broadcasting brought music into millions of homes, creating shared musical experiences on a scale never before possible. The electric guitar, synthesiser, and later digital instruments expanded the range of sounds available to musicians.

D Today, streaming platforms have fundamentally altered how music is distributed and consumed. Artists can reach global audiences without record labels, and listeners have access to virtually the entire history of recorded music. However, these changes have also raised concerns about fair compensation for musicians and the potential homogenisation of musical styles driven by algorithmic recommendations.
